about: Machine source of the PII definition. docs/pii-definition.md is the prose version, and the two must list the same class IDs.

tiers.A: Direct identifiers. Always redacted; no profile can turn them off.
tiers.B: Identifiers that become identifying in context. Redacted by strict; a profile may turn one off.
tiers.C: Quasi-identifier combinations. Documented below, no detector, not promised.
tiers.H: Health content. Kept by strict so the document stays usable; a profile may turn it on.

form_words_about: Words that form labels and headings are made of. A classifier or LLM span made only of these (plus common words and titles), with no digit or @, is a label, not a value, and is kept (labels stay, values go). Extend it for a client's forms.

classes.name: Person name
classes.definition: Any name of a person: full, first, middle, last, nickname or preferred name, initials with a surname, and names in signatures. Patients, relatives, contacts, staff and clinicians alike.
counter_examples: the word hope in 'we hope you feel better'
a drug or product named after a person

classes.name: Social Security number
classes.definition: A US Social Security number in any format, including partial ones (last four digits) and ones written out in words.
examples: nine eight seven, sixty-five, four three two zero
counter_examples: a nine-digit order or part number with no SSN label

classes.name: Taxpayer identification number
classes.definition: An ITIN, EIN or other taxpayer number issued to a person.
counter_examples: a company EIN printed in a letterhead

classes.name: Date linked to a person
classes.definition: Every date more specific than a year in a document about a person: birth, death, visit, admission, payment, signature and expiry dates. A year on its own is kept (HIPAA Safe Harbor allows it).
counter_examples: 2019 on its own
a form revision year

classes.name: Phone number
classes.definition: Any telephone number, with or without country code or extension.
counter_examples: a ten-digit NPI or account number with its own label

classes.name: Fax number
classes.definition: A fax number.

classes.name: Email address
classes.definition: Any email address, including shared or role mailboxes that appear in the document.

classes.name: Street address
classes.definition: A street address: house number, street, unit, PO box. Current, prior and billing addresses alike.
counter_examples: a street name used as a direction with no number, such as 'take Davis Street north'

classes.name: Medical record number
classes.definition: A medical record, chart or patient account number at a care provider.

classes.name: Health plan or member ID
classes.definition: A health plan beneficiary, member, subscriber, policy or group number.
counter_examples: a plan name such as 'PPO Gold'

classes.name: Medicare beneficiary identifier
classes.definition: A Medicare Beneficiary Identifier (11 characters in the CMS format) or an older Medicare claim number.
labels: medicare(?: beneficiary)?(?: id| identifier| number| no\.?)?(?: \(mbi\))?

classes.name: Account number
classes.definition: A bank, billing or other financial account number, including the last four digits on their own.
counter_examples: a dollar amount

classes.name: Payment card number
classes.definition: A credit or debit card number, whether or not its checksum is valid, including the last four digits on their own.

classes.name: Card expiry date
classes.definition: The expiry date of a payment card.

classes.name: Card security code
classes.definition: A card verification code (CVV, CVC, CID).

classes.name: Bank routing number
classes.definition: An ABA routing transit number. It names a bank, not a person, but it is redacted with the account it belongs to.
counter_examples: a bare nine-digit number with no routing label

classes.name: Driver's license number
classes.definition: A driver's license or state ID number, with its state prefix when one is written.

classes.name: Passport number
classes.definition: A passport number.

classes.name: Vehicle identification number
classes.definition: A 17-character vehicle identification number.

classes.name: License plate
classes.definition: A vehicle license plate number.
counter_examples: a vehicle make, model or year

classes.name: IP address
classes.definition: An IPv4 or IPv6 address.
counter_examples: a version string such as version 1.2.3.4

classes.name: Device identifier
classes.definition: A MAC address, device serial number or other device identifier.

classes.name: Web address
classes.definition: Any URL in the document. Portal and profile links often carry a user name.

classes.name: Credential
classes.definition: A user name, password, PIN, API key or security answer.

classes.name: Provider identifier
classes.definition: A National Provider Identifier, DEA number or other clinician registration number. It identifies the clinician named next to it.

classes.name: Other identifying number
classes.definition: The HIPAA catch-all: any other number or code unique to a person or their record, such as a form, claim, case or patient ID.
counter_examples: an order number
a dollar amount
a page number

classes.name: City or town
classes.definition: A city, town or neighborhood, anywhere in the document, including inside an organization's name.

classes.name: State or province
classes.definition: A US state, territory or province, as a name or a postal code.
counter_examples: MI meaning myocardial infarction in a medical history (redacted anyway when it is ambiguous)

classes.name: ZIP or postal code
classes.definition: A ZIP code or postal code, including ZIP+4.
counter_examples: a five-digit dollar amount

classes.name: Age
classes.definition: A person's age at any value.
counter_examples: a duration such as 'three weeks'

classes.name: Sex or gender
classes.definition: A person's recorded sex or gender identity.
counter_examples: pronouns, which are kept

classes.name: Marital status
classes.definition: A person's marital or partnership status.
counter_examples: a relationship word such as 'husband' or 'spouse', which is kept

classes.name: Occupation
classes.definition: A person's job title or occupation.
counter_examples: a clinician's credential such as MD or DO after their name

classes.name: Organization tied to a person
classes.definition: An employer, care provider, pharmacy, school, bank or other named organization in a document about a person.

classes.name: Health content
classes.definition: Diagnoses, diagnosis codes, medications, allergies, procedures, test results and blood type. Off in strict: HIPAA de-identification removes identifiers and keeps clinical content, and the document is useless without it.

tier_c: Rare combinations of Tier B values (for example a small town, an exact age over 89 and an occupation) that single out a person even with every listed class redacted.
Free-text events that only one person matches (for example 'the only cardiologist in town who fell off the ferry last June').
Family structure combined with ages (for example 'two children, ages 12 and 9') once names are gone.
